introduction: Follow evidence of habitation, food and the making of settled places.
learningGoal: Compare what archaeological traces can establish, and what remains uncertain.

steps.heading: Homo sapiens emerges in Africa
steps.note: Source says about 300,000 years ago. Rounded 298,000 BCE is a layout anchor only; it is not a calibrated radiocarbon date.

steps.heading: Evidence of First Peoples in Australia
steps.note: At least 65,000 years ago; 63,000 BCE is only a rounded placement and the earlier extent remains unknown.

steps.heading: People inhabit Monte Verde in southern Chile
steps.note: Calibrated radiocarbon age as described by the nomination; rounded BCE anchor only. The page’s “years ago” reference epoch is not specified.

steps.heading: Communal monuments at Göbekli Tepe
steps.note: Approximate archaeological phase; ritual uses are interpretations, not directly observed facts.

steps.heading: Permanent settlement at Tell es-Sultan
steps.note: Broad ninth–eighth-millennium evidence window; settlement began earlier.

steps.heading: Households cluster at Çatalhöyük
steps.note: Eastern mound occupation only; the western mound continued into a later phase.

steps.heading: Cultivation transforms the Kuk wetlands
steps.note: Approximate 6,500 years-ago statement; rounded 4,500 BCE anchor. Earlier wetland activity is distinct.

steps.heading: Caral’s monumental city takes shape
steps.note: The source’s radiocarbon-based site-development range is approximate; it is not the lifespan of a named dynasty.
